title: Two dyes ride the water
hook: Water carries two dyes up a paper strip, but one clings harder. Where does each end up?

doesNotKnow: that parts of a mixture separate because they cling to the paper by different amounts
that clinging, not weight or darkness, sets how far a dye travels

misconception: The heaviest, or the darkest, colour moves least.
objective: The learner can say that in paper chromatography the dye that clings more to the paper travels a smaller fraction of the water's distance, so it ends lower on the strip.

claims.text: In paper chromatography a solvent (here water) climbs the paper and carries dissolved dyes up with it at different speeds.
claims.source: Harris, Quantitative Chemical Analysis (chromatography principles); Chemistry LibreTexts, Paper chromatography.

claims.text: A dye that clings more strongly to the paper travels less far up the strip than one that clings less.
claims.source: A component more strongly retained by the stationary phase has a smaller retention factor (IUPAC Gold Book 'retention factor' / 'Rf'; Harris, ch. 23).

claims.text: Rf, the retention factor, is the distance the spot travelled divided by the distance the solvent travelled.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'retardation factor (Rf)': Rf = distance moved by the zone / distance moved by the solvent front.

claims.text: In the toy model a dye with stickiness k travels the fraction 1/(1 + k) of the water's distance, so dye A (k = 1) is at 5.0 cm and dye B (k = 3) at 2.5 cm when the water has risen 10 cm.
claims.source: 10 × 1/(1+1) = 5.0 cm; 10 × 1/(1+3) = 2.5 cm; Rf 0.50 and 0.25 (node; Demo.tsx rf(k)). 'Stickiness' is a teaching quantity; the form follows Rf = 1/(1 + retention ratio) for a dye spending k times as long held as moving. Illustrative, not a measured dye.

claims.text: Model: a toy model in which stickiness is a number from 1 to 5; real dyes depend on the paper and solvent.
claims.source: Stage label 'Toy model.' Real Rf values depend on solvent, paper and temperature (Harris).

recall.question: In paper chromatography, a dye with Rf 0.2 and a dye with Rf 0.7 are separated. Which clings more to the paper?
options: neither: Rf depends only on weight
recall.why: A small Rf means the dye travelled a small fraction of the water's distance, because it clings more to the paper.
